keyword: how to verify silver purity at home
angle: Practical home testing methods ranked by reliability, grounded in real counterfeit-prevalence data showing roughly 1 in 5 Silver Eagles tested in 2024 were fake and 43% of coin dealers regularly encounter counterfeit silver
secondary_kw: how to test silver at home

stats.claim: In a survey of U.S. coin dealers, 43.3% reported encountering customers attempting to sell counterfeit Silver American Eagle bullion coins, making it the most counterfeited bullion coin in the market.
Among classic collectible coins, 71.7% of surveyed coin dealers most frequently encountered counterfeit Morgan silver dollars, the highest fake-encounter rate of any coin type in the study.
Analysis of over 38,000 Silver Eagle tests conducted in 2024 found approximately 21% of coins tested were confirmed counterfeits, suggesting roughly 1 in 5 silver coins reaching buyers may be fake.

XRF analysis of silver measured against certified reference standards produces an average deviation of just 0.25 percentage points, making it the most precise non-destructive home-accessible testing method available.
Sterling silver, the most common silver standard in jewelry and flatware worldwide, must contain exactly 92.5% pure silver by weight, with the remaining 7.5% typically composed of copper.

Over 80% of coin dealer survey respondents reported an increase in the number of counterfeit coins and bars entering the marketplace over the prior five years, signaling an accelerating fraud environment.
